evidence.excerpt: Reproducibility in single-cell RNA sequencing analyses depends not only on algorithmic choices but also on the computational environment, including workflow manager, container version, and execution platform. This study ran an identical scRNA-seq clustering pipeline—from raw count matrix to annotated UMAP—using Snakemake, Nextflow, WDL, CWL, and a custom Makefile-based approach across three computational environments: a local HPC cluster, a cloud instance, and a local workstation. The pipeline was applied to two datasets of 8,000 and 22,000 cells. Cell-type cluster assignments were identical across workflow managers within the same environment for deterministic steps but diverged by up to 4.1% of cells in stochastic steps when floating-point rounding behaviour differed between platforms. Conda environment pinning and container-based execution reduced inter-platform divergence to under 0.3% of cells. A minimum specification for reproducible scRNA-seq pipeline reporting was proposed, covering software versions, container hashes, and random seed logging.
